title: Recognize and Use Similar Triangles
description: Identify similar triangles from matching angles, pair corresponding sides, set up proportions, and solve the right-triangle altitude configuration without mentally rotating the triangles.

blocks.html:
Give it a try

Spend about a minute on this question. Keep your first idea, even if you are unsure. You can continue without submitting an answer.

shared_prompt.title: Opening question
shared_prompt.html: Triangle \(JKL\) is similar to triangle \(PQR\), where \(J\), \(K\), and \(L\) correspond to \(P\), \(Q\), and \(R\), respectively. If \(JK=8\), \(KL=12\), and \(PQ=20\), what is the length of \(QR\)?

blocks.html:
Find the matching sides before calculating

The opening question gives side lengths, but the useful ratio depends on which sides correspond. We’ll use Match, Pair, Proportion to make that choice clear.

Start with angle marks so rotation and size do not distract from the matches.

Match the angle marks

Which vertex matches B? Follow the angle marks rather than its location on the page.

figure.alt: Two differently oriented right triangles; matching angles are marked in matching colors
figure.caption: Match the colored angle marks.

content.prompt: In the diagram, which vertex corresponds to vertex \(B\)?
content.hint: Find the angle with the same blue marking as angle \(B\).
content.explanation: The blue angles match, so \(B\leftrightarrow F\). Rotation does not change the correspondence.

figure.alt: Two differently oriented right triangles with matching angle colors: A matches D, B matches F, and C matches E
figure.caption: The two triangles from the opening diagram.

blocks.html:
Same shape gives proportional sides

Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and one scale factor for corresponding sides. Sides correspond when their endpoints match: A↔D and C↔E make AC↔DE.

Two angle matches are enough

AA similarity means angle-angle: two matching angle pairs establish similarity. The third pair also matches because a triangle’s angles total 180°.

content.prompt: Triangle \(PQR\) has \(\angle P=48^\circ\) and \(\angle Q=72^\circ\). Triangle \(XYZ\) has \(\angle X=60^\circ\) and \(\angle Y=48^\circ\). Why can you conclude the triangles are similar?
choices: They both contain a side whose length is labeled with a variable.
Their first-named vertices, \(P\) and \(X\), have equal angles.
Triangles are similar to one another automatically.
They have two matching angle pairs: \(48^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\).
content.hint: Find each triangle's third angle by subtracting its two given angles from \(180^\circ\).
content.explanation: Triangle \(PQR\) has third angle \(60^\circ\), while triangle \(XYZ\) has third angle \(72^\circ\). Two angle pairs match, so AA proves similarity.

shared_prompt.title: Parallel lines and nested triangles
shared_prompt.html: In the diagram, \(DE\parallel BC\). The smaller triangle \(ADE\) sits inside the larger triangle \(ABC\).

blocks.html:
Parallel lines can reveal the matches

The small and large triangles share angle A. Parallel DE and BC give another equal angle pair at D and B. These two pairs establish similarity.

content.prompt: Which angle matches prove \(\triangle ADE\sim\triangle ABC\)?
choices: \(\angle A\) matches itself, and \(\angle ADE=\angle ABC\).
The triangles have no matching angles because one is smaller.
content.hint: Use the shared top angle and one pair made equal by the parallel lines.
content.explanation: The triangles share angle \(A\), and the parallel lines give \(\angle ADE=\angle ABC\). Two equal angle pairs prove AA similarity.

figure.alt: Two differently oriented right triangles with matching angle colors: A matches D, B matches F, and C matches E
figure.caption: The two triangles from the opening diagram.

blocks.html:
Match, Pair, Proportion

  1. Match equal angles or use the stated vertex order.
  2. Pair sides joining matching vertices.
  3. Write two ratios in the same triangle order.
  4. Solve for the missing length.

content.prompt: If \(A\leftrightarrow D\), \(B\leftrightarrow F\), and \(C\leftrightarrow E\), which side corresponds to \(AC\)?
content.hint: Replace endpoint \(A\) with its match and endpoint \(C\) with its match.
content.explanation: \(A\leftrightarrow D\) and \(C\leftrightarrow E\), so side \(AC\leftrightarrow DE\).

blocks.html:
Keep one triangle order

For \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE\), use \(AB/DF=BC/FE\). Both numerators come from ABC. Reversing both ratios also works; reversing only one does not.

content.prompt: Given \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE\), which proportion is valid?
content.hint: Check both the side matches and the direction of each ratio.
content.explanation: \(AB\leftrightarrow DF\) and \(BC\leftrightarrow FE\), with first-triangle sides over second-triangle sides in both ratios.

blocks.html:
Use two matching pairs

If AB=6, DF=9, BC=10, and FE=x, use 6/9=10/x. This gives 6x=90 and x=15. The larger side is 3/2 times its partner.

content.prompt: Again, \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE\). If \(AC=8\), \(DE=12\), \(DF=15\), and \(AB=x\), what is \(x\)?
content.solution:
From \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE\), match letters in order: \(AB\leftrightarrow DF\) and \(AC\leftrightarrow DE\).
Keep the first triangle on top in both ratios: \(\frac{AB}{DF}=\frac{AC}{DE}\), so \(\frac{x}{15}=\frac{8}{12}\).
Simplify the right side to \(\frac{2}{3}\), then \(x=15\cdot\frac{2}{3}=10\).
Check: the first triangle is smaller since \(8<12\), and \(10<15\) fits.
So the answer is choice A, \(10\).
content.explanation: \(x/15=8/12=2/3\), so \(x=10\). Both ratios compare the first triangle with the second.

blocks.html:
Use the same routine inside one triangle

Since \(\triangle ADE\sim\triangle ABC\), AD matches AB and DE matches BC. For AD=6, AB=15, DE=8, BC=x, use 6/15=8/x. Thus x=20.

content.prompt: In the same parallel-lines setup, \(AD=4\), \(AB=10\), \(DE=6\), and \(BC=x\). What is \(x\)?
content.solution:
In the parallel-lines diagram, \(\triangle ADE\sim\triangle ABC\), so \(AD\leftrightarrow AB\) and \(DE\leftrightarrow BC\).
Keep small triangle over large triangle in both ratios: \(\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{DE}{BC}\), so \(\frac{4}{10}=\frac{6}{x}\).
Cross multiply: \(4x=60\), so \(x=15\).
Check: \(BC=15\) is longer than \(DE=6\), which fits the larger triangle.
So the answer is choice C, \(15\).

blocks.html:
An altitude creates another useful diagram

An altitude meets the opposite side at a right angle. Here CD runs from the right-angle vertex C to hypotenuse AB.

Find the right angles and the shared acute angles.

The three right triangles are similar

Each small triangle shares an acute angle with the large triangle and has a right angle. AA applies, so \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle ACD\sim\triangle CBD\).

Choose the two triangles containing the lengths you need.

content.prompt: Why is \(\triangle ACD\) similar to the large triangle \(\triangle ABC\)?
choices: They both have a right angle and share angle \(A\), so AA applies.
They share side \(AC\), so their angles have to match.
Every altitude divides a triangle into congruent triangles.
content.hint: Identify one equal right-angle pair and one acute angle that appears in both triangles.
content.explanation: The right angle at \(C\) in the large triangle corresponds to the right angle at \(D\) in the smaller triangle, and angle \(A\) is shared.

blocks.html:
Keep the same proportion routine

Pick two of the similar triangles. Match their right angles and a shared acute angle, then pair the opposite sides. Keep the ratio order consistent, just as before.

shared_prompt.title: Hypotenuse piece problem
shared_prompt.html: Suppose the large triangle has \(AB=25\) and \(AC=15\). Find \(AD=d\).

blocks.html:
Find a hypotenuse piece

Compare ABC with ACD. Their hypotenuses AB=25 and AC=15 match; AC=15 and AD=d also match. Use 25/15=15/d, giving d=9.

Find the altitude

Compare ACD with CBD. AD=9 matches CD=h, and CD=h matches DB=16. Use 9/h=h/16, giving \(h^2=144\). A length is positive, so h=12.

shared_prompt.title: Right-triangle altitude

content.prompt: In another right-triangle altitude diagram, the hypotenuse pieces are \(4\) and \(9\). If the altitude is \(h\), then \(4/h=h/9\). What is \(h\)?
content.solution:
The proportion \(\frac{4}{h}=\frac{h}{9}\) compares small over medium in each of the two smaller triangles, with the altitude appearing in both.
Cross multiply: \(h^2=4\cdot9=36\).
A length is positive, so \(h=\sqrt{36}=6\).
Check: \(6\) sits between the pieces \(4\) and \(9\), matching its size position.
So the answer is choice A, \(6\).
content.hint: Cross multiply to get \(h^2=36\), then use the positive value because \(h\) is a length.

shared_prompt.title: Right-triangle altitude

blocks.html:
Find a leg of the large triangle

Compare ABC with CBD. AB=25 matches BC=b, and BC=b matches DB=16. Use 25/b=b/16, giving \(b^2=400\), so b=20.

shared_prompt.title: Right-triangle altitude

blocks.html:
Return to the missing side

Try the opening question again. Match the corresponding sides before deciding how to calculate.

content.prompt: Return to the opening question. What answer do you get now?
content.hint: Use the stated vertex matches to pair JK with PQ and KL with QR. Keep both ratios in the same triangle order.
content.explanation: Correspondence gives \(\frac{QR}{KL}=\frac{PQ}{JK}=\frac{20}{8}\), so \(QR=12\cdot\frac{20}{8}=30\), and \(30>12\) passes the size check. Adding the difference \(20-8\) gives \(24\), and \(4.8\) inverts the ratio.
content.solution: Correspondence gives \(\frac{QR}{KL}=\frac{PQ}{JK}=\frac{20}{8}\), so \(QR=12\cdot\frac{20}{8}=30\), and \(30>12\) passes the size check. Adding the difference \(20-8\) gives \(24\), and \(4.8\) inverts the ratio.

content.prompt: How do you set up a missing-side proportion for similar triangles?
choices: Match equal angles, pair their opposite sides, and keep the same triangle order in both ratios.
Match sides by page position, pair their endpoints, and keep the same triangle order in both ratios.
Match equal angles, pair their opposite sides, and reverse the triangle order in just one ratio.
Match equal angles, pair adjacent sides at random, and keep the same triangle order in both ratios.
content.explanation: Correspondence determines the side pairs. Keeping each triangle in the same ratio position preserves the scale factor.

blocks.html:
Try it on your own

Choose the approach for each question. Try these now or save them for homework.

content.prompt: Two triangles have two matching angle pairs. A side of length \(4\) in the smaller triangle corresponds to \(10\) in the larger triangle. Another side of length \(6\) in the smaller triangle corresponds to \(x\). What is \(x\)?
content.explanation: The large-to-small scale factor is \(10/4=5/2\), so \(x=6(5/2)=15\).

shared_prompt.title: Leg length problem
shared_prompt.html: Altitude \(CD\) meets the hypotenuse \(AB\) at \(D\). Given \(AB=18\) and \(DB=8\), find \(BC=x\).

content.prompt: Right triangle ABC has its right angle at C. Altitude CD meets hypotenuse AB at D. If AB=18 and DB=8, what is the length BC?
content.explanation: \(x^2=144\), so the positive side length is \(x=12\). It is shorter than hypotenuse \(18\), which fits.

content.html:
Match, Pair, Proportion

Use the angles to match sides and keep the ratio order consistent.
